I checked the draft against the brand policy and found nothing that needs changing.

- **Claims:** "Certified organic by the Soil Association" matches the allowlist wording exactly. "Plastic-free tea bags" is also on the allowlist. I didn't add "home compostable", and it isn't needed here.
- **Product facts:** The blend name, "caffeine-free", "honeyed" and "20 tea bags" are product facts the product team checks, so they're fine as written.
- **Health claims:** "For the evening" only suggests when to drink it. It doesn't say the tea helps with sleep, relaxation or calm, so it stays on the right side of the line. Don't add wording like "soothing" or "helps you unwind" without checking it against the policy.
- **Other banned content:** There are no superlatives, guarantees, invented numbers, testimonials, urgency or environmental claims beyond section 2.
- **Voice and spelling:** The tone is warm, plain and unhurried, with no banned words, and the spelling is UK.
- **Disclosures:** None are needed on our own product page.

Per section 6, Sam still needs to approve this before it goes live, as with everything public.
